strategy.summary: Reproduce numpy issue #26726 / PR #27014: np.gcd on an object-dtype array containing infinity hangs in the pure-Python _gcd in numpy/_core/_internal.py. Build the buggy commit 619b07c346d9 from source, apply the PR's test_inf_and_nan test, and run only that test under a hard timeout. On the buggy revision the test hangs (killed by timeout) or fails before reaching its assertions; on the fixed revision it passes because _gcd raises ValueError for infinite inputs and TypeError for Python float infinity.

pip_packages: pytest (unpinned; latest stable chosen, no documented constraint)
setuptools (build backend requirements, per requirements/build_requirements.txt at that commit)
system_packages: C and C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
BLAS/LAPACK not required for this test; numpy builds its bundled fallbacks
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy && cd numpy && git checkout 619b07c346d9 && git submodule update --init
git apply /path/to/pr27014_test.patch  (or manually add test_inf_and_nan to class TestGcdLcm in numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py)

strategy.test_command: timeout 120 python -m pytest numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py -k test_inf_and_nan -x -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py::TestGcdLcm::test_inf_and_nan (the PR's added method; it calls np.gcd on np.array([np.inf], dtype=object) with 1, with a Python int 1 on the right, with np.nan, and with float(np.inf) as a Python scalar)
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 619b07c346d9 with the test added: the test does not complete normally. The first assert_raises(ValueError, np.gcd, inf, 1) call hangs inside the pure-Python _gcd loop, so timeout kills pytest (exit 124) and the run counts as a failure; if the hang does not occur, the assertion fails with AssertionError because no ValueError is raised. Fixed revision (PR #27014 head): all four assert_raises calls succeed (three ValueError, one TypeError), pytest reports 1 passed, and exit code is 0. The transition is failure/hang on buggy to pass on fixed.

input_output_examples.input: import numpy as np; inf = np.array([np.inf], dtype=np.object_); np.gcd(inf, 33)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: hang (infinite loop, the call never returns)
input_output_examples.expected_output: ValueError raised with message beginning 'Can only find greatest common demoninator of a'

risks: On the buggy revision the test hangs rather than failing. Always run it under a timeout (the command uses timeout 120); without one the run never terminates. pytest-timeout is an alternative if timeout(1) is unavailable.
The test file path is numpy/_core/tests, which exists only after the core/_core rename. Older commits use numpy/core/tests and the test command will not select the test there.
The environment's test_commands entry (python -c numpy.test()) does not select this test and should not be used; it runs the whole suite and would not isolate the transition.

The failure is pure-Python object-dtype logic. It does not depend on architecture, SIMD, threading, BLAS, or sanitizers, so it should transition on any normal Linux x86_64 or aarch64 build. A C-only fix would need rebuild checks, but the fix is in _internal.py.

pytest and hypothesis have no documented constraint and no era ceiling. This plan chooses the latest stable pytest and does not use hypothesis, since the test is a plain deterministic unit test. Newer pytest versions could change assert_raises-related output but not the pass/fail transition.

NaN handling is not fully specified: the test expects ValueError for np.gcd(np.nan, inf) with inf as an object array, but the expected output for a bare NaN is not stated in the evidence. The test assertion is the oracle.

The issue's reproducer uses 33 as the second argument while the hang description mentions zero. The test uses 1, which the evidence supports as a trigger, so the planned test covers the assertion as written rather than the exact issue pair.

Expected exception types come from assertions written against the fixed code. If the buggy code raises a different exception before hanging, the test may fail with a different message; the transition still holds as a failure on buggy.
Signed zero and subnormal inputs are not covered by any passage and are not planned for.

oracle.reference_source: PR #27014 test diff: test_inf_and_nan in numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py
oracle.why: The test asserts exact exception types (ValueError for infinite object inputs, TypeError for Python float infinity) rather than numerical values, so the oracle is exact.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 619b07c346d9 the first assert_raises(ValueError, np.gcd, inf, 1) call enters the pure-Python _gcd loop with an infinite operand and never returns; the test hangs and timeout kills it, so it fails. If it does return, no ValueError is raised and assert_raises reports AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision _gcd checks math.isfinite on object inputs and raises ValueError for infinite or NaN operands, and raises TypeError for a Python float infinity passed directly; all four assert_raises calls succeed and the test passes.
